column3: Seven-line policy: do not edit vendor/*/src casually, every divergence from upstream must be logged exhaustively in vendor/README.md, tsconfig.json is the only exception.
One-line file containing the single word "AGENTS.md" - a pointer so a Claude-style agent finds the same vendor policy.

Proposed (Status: proposed) staged upgrade of the vendored Cordis stack to rc.11/rc.8/1.1.1, with a PR dependency table, a retire/partial/retain verdict per README modification, and a rule that each PR must migrate every caller of changed Core APIs in the same PR.
Sixteen-line CLI: new Context(), baseUrl from process.cwd(), load the Loader, then loader.create an Include of ./cordis.yml.
Upstream MIT licence text, copyright Shigma, preserved per the vendor policy.
@deepseek-ai/cordis 4.0.5, ESM-only, publishes lib/index.js + lib/types declarations and also src so the ./src/* export map does not point at absent files.
Upstream Cordis README (install, quick start with a Counter service, package table) plus a final Volatile-configuration paragraph documenting that a schema may return Volatile<T> read through .get().

Root/child dependency container; the class is a Proxy whose reads go through the service resolver; extend/isolate/intercept build scoped children without mutating the parent; Context.is brands with the global Symbol.for('cordis.is') so it works across realms and copies.

Event bus mixed onto ctx (on/once/emit/parallel/serial/bail/waterfall); internal/listener is a bail event that can replace a registration, internal/update is a global prepend waterfall, listeners are stored as fiber effects so unload removes them, parallel aggregates rejections.

Plugin lifecycle: FiberState machine, effects, config validation; the effect wrapper is pushed onto the owner list BEFORE setup runs so a reentrant unload awaits setup and cleanup, effectInertia lets an owner join a cleanup another caller started, teardown-notification failures are contained per observer, and await() rethrows the startup error.
Barrel re-exporting context/events/fiber/logger/registry/service/utils plus the Volatile and VolatileSnapshot types from cosmokit.

Structured logging service: named Logger facade, pluggable Exporters, printf-style formatters, a stable colour hash per logger name, and a 1000-message ring buffer of every Message (monotonic sn, timestamp, WeakRef to the owning fiber).

Service resolution layer behind the context proxy: provide/get/set/accessor/mixin, the get trap walks the fiber chain and refuses an inactive injected service, provide notifies dependents and awaits them before deleting its own store entry.

Plugin registry: normalises function/class/object plugins to a callback identity key, tracks one Runtime per callback, Inject decorator for classes and methods, ctx.plugin() returns a thenable whose await() rethrows the startup error.

Base class for named services on ctx; registers itself through reflect.provide so it dies with the owning fiber, [Service.invoke] makes a service callable, [Service.resolveConfig] merges intercept config root-first, and Symbol.hasInstance is overridden because the constructor may be a proxy.

Shared internals: DisposableList with O(1) delete by value, the all-Symbol.for symbol table, prototype joining, traceable proxies that rebind ctx to the caller, and composeError which splices outer call-site frames into a thrown async error's stack.

Extends the repo-root tsconfig.base.json, emits to lib/types, and relaxes noImplicitAny/noImplicitThis/strictFunctionTypes/noUncheckedIndexedAccess/exactOptionalPropertyTypes for this vendored package.
Upstream MIT licence text (Shigma), preserved.
@deepseek-ai/cosmokit 1.8.6, ESM, publishes lib/index.js, the type declarations and src.

Upstream README plus a Config-references section documenting createVolatile/updateVolatile/volatileEntries, the shared-symbol protocol, and the rule that snapshot change must be compared through .get().
Forty-two lines of array helpers - contain, intersection, difference, union, deduplicate, remove (splices in place and reports whether found) and makeArray.
Barrel re-exporting array/types/misc/string/time/volatile.

Shared types and small helpers - Dict, Get, Extract, MaybeArray, Promisify, Awaitable, Intersect, isNullable, isPlainObject, filterKeys, mapValues/valueMap, pick, omit, and a defineProperty that always creates a non-enumerable property.

Case and path helpers - capitalize/uncapitalize, camelCase, a hand-written tokenizer behind paramCase/snakeCase that handles HTTPServer correctly, the camelize/hyphenate runtime aliases and type-level twins, formatProperty, trimSlash, sanitize.

The Time namespace - ms-to-week constants, a settable timezone offset, getDateNumber/fromDateNumber, parseTime for strings like 3d2h, parseDate, a humanising format(ms) and the template() date pattern renderer.

Runtime type predicates with a toStringTag fallback, the Binary namespace (base64/hex), a cycle-safe clone that preserves prototypes and descriptors, and deepEqual - which treats two volatile references as equal regardless of their snapshots, compares URLs by href and opaque objects by identity.

The volatile config reference - createVolatile takes a detached frozen copy (rejecting functions, cycles and non-plain objects), updateVolatile commits a candidate snapshot into a live reference, volatileEntries enumerates references and their object-key paths; the write symbol is Symbol.for so it crosses ESM/CJS copies.
Extends the root base config, emits to lib/types, relaxes noUncheckedIndexedAccess/exactOptionalPropertyTypes/noImplicitOverride/unused-locals; the leaf of the vendored project-reference graph.
Upstream MIT licence text, preserved.
@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-group 1.0.5, ESM, peer-depends on the loader and cordis workspaces.
Upstream README - a group entry is always enabled itself but disabling it stops its children, and nested entry ids use colon separators (tools:logger).
Three-line re-export - import { Group } from the loader package and export it as the default plugin.
Extends the root base config, emits to lib/types, with project references to ../cordis and ../loader.
Upstream MIT licence text, preserved.
@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-hmr 1.0.20, ESM; deps chokidar, picomatch, @babel/code-frame, schemastery; esbuild is a dev dependency only for its imported BuildFailure type.
Upstream README - the watcher, canonicalisation of the watch base directory, the --expose-internals requirement (the plugin throws without it) and the hmr/change and hmr/reload events.
Thirty-six lines turning an esbuild BuildFailure into a readable log - for each error with a location it reads the source file and renders a @babel/code-frame frame with the message highlighted.

Hot module replacement over Node's internal loader - watch, trace the module graph, classify changes accepted/declined, back up and clear BOTH the ESM loadCache and the CJS require.cache (via Map.prototype.delete because Node 24 only clears the type slot), re-import, swap the plugin registration, and roll back both caches on failure; externals trigger a full loader.exit().
Extends the root base config and declares project references to six vendored packages - cosmokit, cordis, loader, include, timer, schemastery.
Upstream MIT licence text, preserved.
@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-include 1.0.10, ESM, peer-depends on the loader and cordis workspaces, depends on js-yaml.
Upstream README - the file-backed tree, the four config fields (path, initial, patches, enableLogs) and the patch semantics (insert entries, or override fields on entries with a matching id).

File-backed loader tree - exports the pure applyEntryPatches and the entryListSchema YAML dialect so dsh --dump-config cannot drift from what boots; patches structuredClone their input and index inserted rows; a non-array file is one invalid-file signal; initial is used only after ENOENT; writes are atomic with a 10-attempt rename retry on EACCES/EBUSY/EPERM; refresh() keeps the last good tree on error.
Extends the root base config and references ../cosmokit, ../cordis, ../loader.
Upstream MIT licence text, preserved.
@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader 1.0.6, ESM, peer-depends on cordis and optionally node-addon-require-builtin@^0.1.9 (the native helper used to reach Node's internal loader).

Upstream README with the Entry API table plus a dense Volatile-configuration section stating the whole contract and its limits - a transform that builds a fresh instance per parse always takes the remount, and a throwing volatile-update listener is logged but does not fail the update.

equalExceptVolatile compares two raw configs using schema metadata without executing expressions, validators or the internal/config waterfall; a missing object node compares against its declared default, unknown fields and schema back-edges keep strict raw equality.

One configured plugin node - import, start, update, pause, dispose; a config change that is volatile-only is committed into the running references without a remount (checked by equalExceptVolatile plus ACTIVE-state and unchanged-context guards) and emits loader/volatile-update; moduleNamespace keeps the raw import result for HMR; disabled may be a !!js expression evaluated at every mount decision.

EntryGroup owns a list of child entries; Group is the plugin that mounts one; EntryGroup.key = Symbol.for('cordis.group') is the tree-carrier marker the Loader's internal/config hook uses to keep a carrier's config literal.

Per-entry service isolation - LocalRealm per entry, GlobalRealm per label, a per-entry delim symbol that decides whether an implementation may be transferred, and realm garbage collection on partial dispose.

Abstract EntryTree - create/update/remove/resolve with colon-separated nested ids, import through the internal loader with composeError, and getTasks()/await() which collect every pending import or fiber inertia task across the whole tree as one settle query.
Thirty-two lines holding the !!js expression dialect - a new Function evaluator with a with(ctx) scope, a recursive interpolate, and the isJsExpr guard.

The Loader service - owns an EntryTree, imports plugin modules and keeps the graph in sync; the internal/config waterfall interpolates expressions but returns the config literal for tree carriers, the internal/update waterfall writes simplify() output back with its schema receiver, and the internal/plugin observer resolves self-disposal into options.disabled after distinguishing six disposal cases.

Typed access to Node's internal ESM loader (v1 and v2 shapes documented) - fromInternal() classifies the loader by which module-job API it owns, never by Node version, because v2 landed in 24.12.0 and a major-version test mistags 24.0-24.11.1; an unrecognised loader is left unclassified rather than guessed.
Extends the root base config, emits to lib/types, and references ../cosmokit, ../cordis, ../schemastery.
Build override - one ESM entry re-bundled from lib/types/index.js to lib/ with codeSplitting off, dts off and clean off (it must not wipe the tsc output).
Upstream MIT licence text, preserved.
@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-logger-console 1.0.5 - a two-entry package whose exports map selects lib/index.js under the node condition and lib/browser.js by default.
Upstream README with the config table and the note that the Node entry uses node:util.inspect for %o/%O while the browser entry passes arguments straight to console.
Browser entry - re-exports shared.ts and dispatches to console.error/warn/log with a [E] name prefix, passing the raw args through.
Node entry - re-exports shared.ts, overrides the %o/%O formatters with node:util.inspect (depth Infinity, compact) and derives the default colour level from supports-color.

Shared console exporter - renders a Message into a colour-coded, timestamped, width-padded line, and declares the same config fields in a schemastery schema so the settings UI can be generated from it.
Extends the root base config, emits to lib/types, and references ../cosmokit, ../cordis, ../schemastery.
Build override producing two single-entry passes (index and browser) so the shared base class is inlined into each instead of being split into a hash-named chunk.

The vendor manifest (package, upstream repo, version, commit) plus the exhaustive 24-entry local-modification log with the reasoning for each divergence and the upstream sync procedure - including the reentrant-disposal hardening, the capability-based Node loader detection and the whole volatile-config subsystem.
Upstream MIT licence text, preserved.

@deepseek-ai/schemastery 3.18.5, dual format - main to lib/index.cjs, module to lib/index.mjs, exports selecting import/require - because without conditional exports a module-hook host can race the CJS entry's require of ESM Cosmokit.

Upstream README covering every type, the instance methods, validation options, shorthand syntax, extensibility and serialisability, plus a final Volatile-configuration section on .volatile() and its supported placements.

The schema validator every plugin Config uses - a callable/constructible Schema with a Standard Schema v1 interface, per-type resolvers, UI metadata (role, description, defaults, min/max/step, badges), validateVolatileSchema which rejects a volatile field without a fixed object path, and simplify() which strips default-valued fields for persistence; kSchema and kValidationError are global symbols so a foreign copy is still recognised.
Extends the root base config, emits to lib/types, uses module preserve, and references ../cosmokit.
Build override producing both formats and pinning the extensions (.mjs for es, .cjs for cjs) so the package keeps the main/module split its manifest declares.
Upstream MIT licence text, preserved.
Five-line locale file - the English Settings-plugin inventory title "timer".
Six-line locale file - the Chinese title and description for the timer service in the Settings plugin inventory.
@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-timer 1.1.7, ESM, exports ./locale/*.json and publishes the locale directory alongside lib and src.
Upstream README with the API table and the statement that timer handles are registered on the current fiber and cleared when that fiber is disposed.

Disposal-aware timers - timeout/interval/throttle/debounce are registered as ctx effects so they die with the fiber; the async-iterator interval form rejects a pending next() with a disposal error; the service mixes its methods onto ctx.
Extends the root base config, emits to lib/types, and references ../cosmokit and ../cordis.

CI performance gate - includes benchmarks/**/*.bench.ts and .bench.client.ts, runs fileParallelism off with maxWorkers 1 so a measurement never shares the CPU, 600 s timeout, and a globalSetup that clears timings and renders the scaling report.

The root unit/coverage lane - the whole test inventory, the thread-safe and process-bound projects (everything forks, because Node 24 has aborted in the CJS lexer from worker threads), explicit platform exclusion lists, a v8 per-file 100% threshold, and a coverage partition mode that disables the gate so CI can shard the run.

Real-API e2e lane - loads the root .env, retries twice for transient quota flakes, bounds the worker pool through DSH_E2E_MAX_WORKERS (1 restores serial), and excludes the *.expected.e2e.ts files that live in their own config.
Owner-local assembled expected-output lane - includes apps/cli/tests/**/*.expected.e2e.ts only, with a 120 s timeout and maxWorkers min(5, availableParallelism()).

The two things every source-mode config shares - vitestExecArgv (--no-webstorage when the flag is negatable) and standardDecoratorPlugin, a pre Vite plugin that transpiles standard TS decorators and injects the v8 ignore comments the 100% gate needs.

Snapshot corpus lane - replay is the keyless default and loads no .env, record loads it (and rethrows a non-ENOENT failure); replay runs files in parallel while record and refresh stay serial because refresh writes back volatile values from fixtures already on disk.
Opt-in browser performance lane for apps/web/stress-tests/**/*.stress.ts - 600 s timeouts and no file parallelism; no default config includes *.stress.ts.
Web browser lane - real host entry points, built-client interaction snapshots and replayed keyless e2e scenarios, plus the inspector client-browser e2e; 180 s timeout, serial.

Manual high-cardinality diagnostics lane - spreads vitest.web.config.ts and adds --expose-gc for forced-GC memory baselines; includes apps/web/tests/**/*.perf.ts and the conversation UI perf client specs.
Four lines ignoring node_modules, .cache, .dist and .generated - the disposable projected-doc and build trees.

Keeps native code-group radios from interfering - each tab strip is rewritten into its own form so a search excerpt cannot clear the page's selection, plus an MPA-only stylesheet that exposes every block when the theme client handlers are absent.

VitePress site configuration - per-locale sidebars and nav derived from the manifest, the wordmark inlined so currentColor follows the theme, a hidden-until-scrolling sidebar scrollbar driven by a capture-phase listener, Vue-interpolation escaping in text and inline code, and a production-only fence render cache.
Ten lines - a focus-visible ring on the code-group radio label and a rule forcing every block visible inside the local search box, which has no tab controls.
Two-line ambient declaration, declare module '*.css', so the theme can import its stylesheets.

Enhances standalone loaded images with a fullscreen trigger without moving or replacing them - a MutationObserver plus load/error listeners, a strict eligibility predicate (own paragraph, non-empty alt, not linked/inline/decorative/hidden/mermaid/no-zoom), and removal of the enhancement when src/srcset/currentSrc changes.

Theme entry - extends the default theme, lazily imports the mermaid/image/media viewers on mount, re-scans them on route, language and theme change, and renders PageMarkdownActions in the doc-before slot keyed by route + language + raw path.

149 lines styling the shared viewer - a 44 px trigger button, the floating rounded toolbar with a tabular-nums scale label, absolute viewport insets, a 600 px breakpoint, and the image trigger at the container's bottom-right.

Shared full-screen modal, focus trap and pan/zoom controller - the content lives in an open shadow root so a Mermaid clone cannot resolve its styles or fragment IDs against the original, the Tab key cycles the controls in a fixed order, arrow keys pan by 64/scale pixels, and cleanup is idempotent and also runs on setup failure.

Adds a fullscreen trigger to each rendered Mermaid SVG - it waits for an SVG with a usable viewBox, clones it into the shared viewer, and removes or re-adds the trigger when the container's SVG is replaced.
144 lines styling the copy button and chevron split control, the dropdown menu (18 px radius, 360 px max width), the status line and the pre-hydration static link.

Per-page copy-page-as-Markdown and view-as-Markdown actions - the clipboard write starts inside the click gesture with the pending fetch promise handed to ClipboardItem, the request is aborted on unmount and on route/locale change, request failure and clipboard failure are distinct states, and the server-rendered output is a plain link so it works before hydration.

23 lines - website/ owns only VitePress configuration, presentation assets and the publication manifest, the projector writes disposable Markdown to the ignored .generated/, and a gate rejects additional non-ignored Markdown under website/.

Production doc-site build with project-owned output preparation - cleanDocSiteOutput refuses an output whose lexical path or nearest existing parent escapes the real site root and unlinks a link-shaped output instead of traversing its target, running after VitePress resolves the config and before it writes.

The canonical publication manifest - pairedPages projects one canonical Markdown into two locale route trees (foo.md English, foo.zh.md Chinese) without copying prose, sectionSpec throws when a sidebar section has no declared placement, and landingLink derives nav targets from the collection's first page.

Private unpublished @deepseek-ai/website package - dev/build/preview scripts over VitePress, with tsx build.ts as the build so the project-owned output preparation runs, and pinned dev dependency versions.
Three-line 50x50 SVG logo (a single long path) - the site favicon, linked from the VitePress head with the site's base prefix.

19-line 143x23 SVG wordmark whose paths all use fill=currentColor - the reason the config inlines it rather than using an img, which would freeze the mark's colours; the logo mark is clipped by a dsh-wordmark-clip path.

52 lines of dev middleware serving a route's raw Markdown and llms.txt while leaving Vite's Markdown module imports alone - it inspects sec-fetch-dest so script/style/image requests always fall through, and an explicit ?dsh-raw=1 fetch of an unpublished route returns 404.

Proves a search excerpt cannot clear the page's code-group selection - the page radios and the excerpt share the generated radio name but the assertion is on the FORM boundary, and the MPA fallback is verified by measuring getComputedStyle before and after injecting it.

Three-line file-snapshot of the English image viewer - the trigger button, the full dsh-media-viewer dialog markup with its toolbar and 63% scale label, and the cloned img with its absolute centring style.
The Chinese counterpart of the image-viewer snapshot (全屏查看图片 / 缩小 / 放大 / 适应窗口 / 查看器帮助 / 关闭).

One-line file-snapshot of the mounted English copy control - the Copy page button with aria-disabled/aria-busy false, the More page actions toggle bound to aria-controls, and an empty role=status region.
The Chinese counterpart of that snapshot - identical structure with 复制页面 / 更多页面操作 labels.

One-line file-snapshot of the English dropdown in its open state - aria-expanded true, the role=menu container labelled Page actions, and the two menuitems (Copy page with a description, View as Markdown as a link).
The Chinese counterpart of the open-menu snapshot (页面操作; /guide/quickstart.md).
One-line file-snapshot of the pre-hydration English output - a single link to /deepseek-harness/en/guide/quickstart.md with target=_blank and an external-link icon, and no buttons at all.
The Chinese counterpart of the pre-hydration snapshot, linking /deepseek-harness/guide/quickstart.md.

Image viewer contract - a mocked panzoom, a fake HTMLDialogElement.showModal that focuses the autofocus element, and assertions that the document HTML is byte-identical after installation for linked/decorative/inline/grouped/failed images, plus file-snapshot and cleanup-on-refresh/dispose/remove/error coverage.

Mermaid viewer contract - a mocked panzoom and a viewBox getter spy; asserts the shadow-root clone still references url(#arrow) while the document holds exactly one #diagram, that the fit scale recomputes on resize (0.2 then 0.15), and that a replaced diagram closes the open view.

Copy/view actions - a deferred() helper that records pending work so afterEach can reject it, a mocked vitepress useData/useRoute, and a fake DefaultTheme.Layout rendering only the doc-before slot; asserts the clipboard write starts during the click, the pending state is aria-busy rather than disabled, and a late response is aborted and cannot report success on the next page.

Dev middleware contract - a mocked rawMarkdownRoute and a fake request/response pair; the sec-fetch-dest table is the whole policy (script/style/image always delegate), an unparseable target is delegated, an unpublished route 404s only for an explicit raw fetch, and a projection error propagates instead of becoming an empty success.
